art.title: A Gentleman in Adoration before the Madonna
art.why: An ordinary man in his own clothes, hands together in prayer: a lay person's daily prayer, which is what the examen is. Not evening (none of the NGA prayer scenes is set at evening; Dou's Hermit was taken by reason-and-revelation).

art.title: Moonlight
art.why: A path under trees in hazy moonlight: a night scene, for the dark night, without a melodramatic subject.

art.title: The Road in the Woods
art.why: An adult and a child walk away from us along a road into the woods: going on, together, a step at a time. Not 'at dawn': the description gives a light-blue sky only.

memory.title: Speak, for your servant hears
memory.source: WEB: 'Yahweh came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak; for your servant hears.”' https://ebible.org/eng-web/1SA03.htm

memory.title: Be transformed
memory.source: WEB: 'Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.' https://ebible.org/eng-web/ROM12.htm

flags: No NGA paintings for sessions 1–3 (Samuel, Teresa, Ignatius); session 5 has none in the spec. Four sessions without a painting.

Rules for discernment: the spec's 'First Week 1–14' are Exercises 313–327 in the standard numbering; Mullan's edition does not print the paragraph numbers, so give the standard numbers in refs and say so.
E. Allison Peers is not used anywhere: Teresa is Stanbrook/Zimmerman and John of the Cross is Lewis/Zimmerman.
Ignatius's Principle and Foundation is read in reformation: point back, don't read it again.
The Newman URL is unconfirmed (search limit): see its source note.
No music is set in the spec. Possible additions, if wanted: 'be-thou-my-vision' (session 7) or 'dear-lord-and-father' (session 1, 'still small voice'), but silence uses the latter.
